newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 27.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 27. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Five Indonesian tycoons who hold substantial shares in automobile manufacturer PT Astra Internasional said on Tuesday there was no need to restructure the company. Together Putera Sampoerna, Anthony Salim, Bob Hasan, Prajogo Pangestu and Usman Admadjaja own over 50 percent of Astra, the country's largest automobile manufacturer.

Satellite-based telecoms service operators must form joint ventures with state-owned satellite companies if they want to serve the Indonesian market, director general of Post and Telecommunications Djakaria Purawidjaja said.
Lawyers of a 13-year-old boy who died while serving an eight-year jail sentence for murder have said they will sue prison authorities if it is found that poor conditions led to the boy's death.

Home Minister Yogie Memet said controversial comments made by Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo in German Magazine Der Spiegel had not been fully explained and the matter was not yet over. Belo denied saying Indonesia treated East Timorese like "scabby dogs" and "slaves" at a press conference in Dili on Monday.

Four members of a consortium which plans to build a toll road from Waru to Perak in East Java have pulled out due to financial difficulties. The consortium is headed by PT Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada, a company headed by President Suharto's daughter Siti Hardianti Rukmana.
